# Conditional Process Plan

A reusable planning definition for payment-process clauses. It inherits connection planning and can add a condition-controlled payment gate. It produces state, channel and handler declarations; producing a plan does not itself perform a payment.

`requestPolicy`, `policyAction`, `policyWatches` and `requestStep` are extension hooks whose bodies are unspecified here. They supply the policy, action name, additional watched paths and request step. Consequently, this definition does not establish a particular payment operation, actor or completed payment outcome.

## Conditional policy

`plan` first builds the inherited connection plan. If the policy's `mode` is absent, this check defaults to `workflow`; any mode other than `when` returns the connection plan without conditional additions.

For `mode: when`, the action name returned by `policyAction` determines an `<action>Allowed` field under `/paymentProcess_{clauseKey}`. The plan initializes that field to `false` and puts its pointer in the corresponding `<action>Gate` field of `/paymentTerms`. An existing different gate pointer causes `PAYMENT_POLICY_GATE_CONFLICT`.

Generated handlers evaluate the gate as true only when all these requirements hold:

- `/activation/active` is exactly `true`.
- Either `/clauses/documentSources` is absent, or `/sourceLinks/ready` is exactly `true`.
- The policy's `when` expression evaluates to exactly `true`.

The handler replaces the gate only if its value changes, then runs the step supplied by `requestStep`. That step runs even when the gate was unchanged; its own behavior determines whether a request is emitted. A true gate establishes this predicate result, not payment completion or a particular person's permission.

Handlers watch the paths returned by `policyWatches` and the static document references found in `when`. A nonempty `parameters.sources`, which defaults to `{}`, also adds an Embedded Node Channel handler without a `sourcePath` filter. The unspecified hook determines which additional changes, including any activation or readiness changes, are watched.

The predicate scanner accepts `$document`, `$nodeBlueId`, `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$and`, `$or`, `$not`, `$exists`, `$includes`, `$size`, `$add`, `$subtract`, `$literal`, `list` and `val`. Other keys cause `PAYMENT_PREDICATE_REQUIRES_STATIC_PURE_DEPENDENCIES`. `$literal` contents are not scanned. `$document` requires a literal, non-root JSON Pointer; references beginning `/sources/` require the alias to be declared in `parameters.sources`. `$nodeBlueId` requires an object containing only `$document`. Invalid references produce the corresponding static-path, static-identity or undeclared-source rejection. Traversal is bounded to 33 scanning levels; remaining nodes cause `PAYMENT_PREDICATE_TOO_DEEP`.

## Inherited connection behavior

Actions come from `type.actions`, or from `parameters.actions` when `type.configurableActions` is exactly `true`. Clause `bindings` override `type.defaultBindings`. Property bindings must satisfy `type.bindingTypes`; a `pointer` binding must be a non-root JSON Pointer. `type.optionalBindings` permits listed bindings to be absent, while action bindings and `type.childActions` are distinguished from property bindings. Actions must be an object unless structural `type.initialState` allows an empty action set.

`type.initialState` contributes object initialization at declared pointer bindings. `type.embeds` and `type.embedsCollections` declare embedded document and collection locations. `type.snapshotBindings` captures available bound values during planning and rejects a bound snapshot whose value is missing. Generated parameter constants normally copy clause parameters except `actions`, `conditions`, `conditionGroups` and `connectionProfiles`; `type.readParametersFromDocument: true` leaves those constants empty. `type.actionDefinition`, when present, selects the generated Compute definition. Executable configuration remains literal data during planning.

Each action binding is a dictionary of named connections. Supported `on` values are `workflow`, `event`, `channel`, `change`, `embedded`, `collection`, `initialized`, `activated` and `timer`. `initialized` selects Clauses Initialized; `activated` selects Document Activated. Change and embedded sources require non-root paths. Collection handlers additionally check that the event's `sourcePath` is below the configured collection path. Embedded and collection sources contribute embedding unless `embed` is `false`. An action's `automatic` connection uses the reserved name `_automatic`. Clause, action and connection names must be nonempty and contain no dot, slash or tilde; unsupported connection fields and invalid option types are rejected.

A connection `profile` resolves through `parameters.connectionProfiles`. Profiles may contain only `params` and `when`; a profiled connection cannot also supply either field locally. `once` defaults to `false`, and connection `when` defaults to `true`. A false connection condition skips execution. Per-action `parameters.conditions` defaults to `true`; applicable `conditionGroups` are also required, with a missing group `condition` defaulting to `false`. A group's `inputs` can be exposed as `conditionInputs`. Conditions referring to unknown actions are rejected.

Workflow connections target `party`, falling back to `channel`, and require a valid authenticated-channel binding name. This declaration does not itself establish the current viewer's authority. Parameters merge action `defaults`, request input when `input: true`, and connection `params`, in that order. Existing values selected by `inputParams` and then `documentParams` override their target paths. Both mappings require non-root JSON Pointers. With `requireExactDocumentVersion: true`, the call must explicitly carry that requirement or fail with `EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`.

After the connection condition passes, generated execution validates action arguments, the action's `require.when`, and action conditions. Failures reject the attempt. Optional `preflight` must report `acceptedNew`, `duplicate`, `rejected` or `skipped`; only `acceptedNew` proceeds to connection `before` steps and action `do`. With `resultContract: outcome-v1`, the action must report one of the same outcomes, and only `acceptedNew` proceeds to `after` steps and the `once` marker. The default `legacy` contract does not impose that explicit outcome check. These outcomes describe local action handling, not confirmation of an external payment.

Each connection has an entry keyed by `actionName.connectionName` under `/connectionState_{clauseKey}`, initialized with `armed: false` and `fired: false`. For `once: true`, `fired` becomes true only at the end of this execution path and suppresses later attempts. For other connections it is not an execution counter. Missing state is unknown; initialization values apply only after initialization is applied.

The inherited pre-activation channel resolver rejects unknown actions or connections, shared `channel` sources and `timer` sources. Workflow resolution returns no generated source channels; other supported sources resolve to their generated channel.

## Timers and transitions

A timer requires exactly one of `timestamp` and `afterEvent`. An absolute `timestamp` is an integer Unix-microsecond instant from 0 through 9007199254740991, arms on `initialized`, and cannot include `delayMs` or `policy`. A relative timer uses its triggering input's timestamp plus `delayMs` milliseconds; `delayMs` must be a positive integer no greater than 9007199254740, and the resulting deadline must fit the timestamp range. Its `afterEvent` cannot be `initialized`.

Relative timer `policy` defaults to `first`, which suppresses further arming once `armed` is true. `latest` permits replacement of the pending keyed request. A supplied `cancelOn` must name a nonempty supported source and emits a cancellation request. The generated code does not clear `armed` on cancellation or firing, so it is not a reliable indication that a timer remains pending. A completed `once` connection also suppresses further arming.

Timer requests use the key `connection` within their generated timer channel. Only committed effects register or cancel timers, and processing requires the specified Time runtime. A request is not a firing; processing may occur later than the requested deadline. Replacement or cancellation cannot undo an earlier firing in logical input order.

`validateConfiguration` calls inherited connection validation and `requestPolicy`, then returns the inherited result; detailed structural checks also occur during planning. `validateTransition` always rejects with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`.
